changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 2 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6296-conditionbuilder-subject-vocabulary.md`

- names `flow-scope.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/flow-scope.ts` — edited by this change

  > The builder built every row subject as `record.` + field name, plus a fixed `record.id` / `user.*` / `org.*` context list. That is correct for all five files that mount it today — six mount sites, since `ActionDefaultInspector` mounts it twice — because every one of them is a record-scoped site. It is wrong for a **flattened**-scoped site such as the flow designer's entry condition, where the trigger record's fields *are* the top-level evaluation context (bare `status`) and the prior values arrive as `previous.FIELD`. This repo's own `flow-scope.ts` already computes that distinction (`fieldPrefix: onStart ? '' : 'record.'`, `includePrevious`), and objectstack's `packages/formula/src/validate.ts` defines the two scopes.

### `.changeset/flow-entry-condition-builder.md`

- names `flow-scope.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/flow-scope.ts` — edited by this change

  > The builder is given the trigger record's own vocabulary — bare field names and `previous.ANGLE-BRACKETS(field)`, resolved by `flow-scope.ts` — rather than the record-scoped default its five other consumers use, so the subjects it offers are the spelling this surface evaluates and teaches. 15 of the 17 entry conditions shipped in the example apps now open as structured rows; the remaining two mix `&&` with a parenthesised `||` group, which is a grammar limit of the row model and keeps them on raw mode by design.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Angle-bracketed names in the quoted prose above are rewritten as `ANGLE-BRACKETS(name)`: GitHub deletes tag-shaped fragments from a stored body, and a quote that silently loses the identifier it is about is worse than a visible repair.

Compared the checked-out tree with `e119f120c` (merge-base with origin/main): 9 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1741 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2345 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36555392560)

### ① Derived judgments

Judged against the binding direction, triage `5881571573`.

1. **The picker shows an action's `description` — RIGHT.** `connectorActionsToOptions` maps each action's `description` onto a new optional `hint` of the module-private `Option` interface (not exported). Only a non-blank string yields a hint; a missing, blank or non-string value (a locale map, say) yields none, and the `datalist` option renders `label — hint` or the label alone. That is the pin "the picker shows the description when authored and nothing when not". The served type is `description?: string` (`ConnectorActionDescriptor`), so the string-only accept set drops nothing the descriptor can carry. Pinned as a unit (`FlowReferenceField.connector.test.ts`) and through the real `ReferenceCombobox` render path with the registry fetch mocked (`FlowReferenceField.actionDescription-11028.test.tsx`, a described and an undescribed action on the same mount).
2. **`nodeOutputRefs` gains a `connector_action` branch — RIGHT.** It sits after the `approval` branch and uses the same `add` (group `outputs`, `detail` the node label), offering `nodeId.key` for each top-level `properties` key of the action's `outputSchema`. The schema is read from the registry by `connectorActionOutputSchema`, whose lookup is the twin of `connectorActionInputSchema` (same shape, same misses resolve to undefined), and the keys by `connectorActionOutputKeys` (plain-object check on the schema and on `properties`; nested `properties` are not descended; empty-string keys dropped). No registry, no committed pair, no schema, no `properties`, or a non-object `properties` offers nothing. Keys are never guessed. Pins: two properties give `post.ts` and `post.channel`; `chat.delete` with no schema gives none; `resolveFlowScope` offers them downstream, never at the connector node itself, and never without the registry.
3. **Where the pair is read — RIGHT.** `committedConnectorAction` reads `connectorConfig.connectorId` and `connectorConfig.actionId`, the same block the existing #4305 read in `FlowNodeInspector` uses, and is type-gated to `connector_action` (an `http` node carrying the same block offers nothing, pinned).
4. **Threading the registry — RIGHT.** `nodeOutputRefs(node, connectors?)`, `resolveFlowScope(draft, nodeId, locale?, connectors?)` and `useFlowScope(draft, nodeId, extraRefs?, connectors?)` each take an optional trailing argument; every existing call site compiles unchanged (Type Check green) and behaves as before without it (pinned). `useFlowScope` adds `connectors` to its memo deps; `useConnectorRegistry` returns a `useState` array, stable until a fetch lands, so the memo does not thrash.
5. **The registry reads — RIGHT, inside the claimed surface.** `FlowNodeInspector` widens its one `useConnectorRegistry` gate to "own committed pair OR `hasCommittedConnectorAction(draft)`", one read for two consumers; `FlowEdgeInspector` gains the same gated read, and both hooks sit above its `!edge` early return. A flow with no committed connector action never fetches for scope (pinned: `fetch` not called). `hasCommittedConnectorAction` reads top-level `nodes` only, the same set `resolveFlowScope` walks, so the gate and the walk agree.
6. **Through the real wiring.** `FlowNodeInspector.connectorOutputRefs-11028.test.tsx` drives both inspectors with the registry fetch mocked and reads the scope-aware "not in scope" note: judged in scope with a declared `outputSchema`, still flagged without one (lit control on the same draft), for a downstream node and a downstream edge guard.
7. **Public surface — none moves** (see ②). New module-level exports from `flow-scope.ts`: `hasCommittedConnectorAction`, `connectorActionOutputSchema`, `connectorActionOutputKeys`. Nothing under `inspectors/` is reachable from the package entry.
8. **Not delivered, correctly.** No change to the served descriptor, the spec or objectstack; no connector-trigger work. The changeset text scopes the "not in scope" relief to the node and edge inspectors' note, not to the Problems panel, which matches what the diff does (③ F1).

- **D2** `FlowEdgeInspector` gains a registry read and `FlowNodeInspector` widens its own, rather than a self-fetch in `useFlowScope`: inside the claim's "plumbing ... inside `metadata-admin/inspectors/`". Accepted. Cost: one extra GET on edge selection in a flow that holds a committed connector action; nothing for any other flow.
- **D3** six `pnpm check:*` gates read at `f0e7aadc7`, one commit before the head: the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts here and are green; the stated delta (a test fixture's locale type) is consistent with the file list. Accepted.
- **D4, D5** an ablation rerun and two write-pace retries: procedural, no bearing on the diff.

Out-of-scope findings, three:
- **F1 Problems panel vs inspectors: HONEST OUT-OF-SCOPE, ESCALATED, NOT A BLOCKER.** Measured at the head: `flowExpressionProblems` is pure, calls `resolveFlowScope(draft, nodeId)` and `resolveFlowScope(draft, source)` with no registry, and is reached through `buildFlowProblems` in `previews/`. Its unknown-reference verdict is `level: 'warning'` (`checkCel`), so the row is an amber badge and a panel row; `deriveInvalidElements` paints errors only, and nothing is gated on it. This diff does not touch that pass, so the panel's row on `post.ok` after the PR is the same row it produced before: a false positive against the engine, which does write `post.ok`. What the PR introduces is the disagreement (two surfaces that were wrong together are now one right and one wrong), not the wrong verdict. Closing it needs a registry at `flowExpressionProblems`, a new read site at its `previews/` caller, outside the claimed inspectors/ surface and outside triage's direction, which named the picker and `nodeOutputRefs`. Ruling: does not block this PR and needs no in-PR fix; the seat files a follow-up card with the dev's dedupe words, serial behind this PR.
- **F2 an edge guard is blind to its source node's own outputs: HONEST, PRE-EXISTING, NOT MADE WORSE.** Both surfaces anchor an edge at `edge.source` (the "#1934" anchor in `FlowEdgeInspector`; `resolveFlowScope(draft, source)` in `flowExpressionProblems`), and `resolveFlowScope` skips `id === nodeId`, so a node's outputs have never been offered on its own out-edge for any node type, approval `nodeId.decision` included. The diff changes neither anchor; the connector branch joins that class. Whether the engine evaluates out-edge guards after the write-back is an objectstack measurement this diff does not depend on. Ruling: a follow-up card for the seat on the edge-scope anchor, not this PR's.
- **F3** the duplicated eight-line registry lookup, kept apart for the React and palette import boundary: recorded in the PR's Acceptance notes; accepted, no action.
